'''Tōtsu Ayume Maguwashi Hime''' (遠津年魚眼眼妙媛, birth and death dates unknown) was an ancient figure in {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}.
== Genealogy ==
Her father was {{ill|Arakawato Hime|ja|荒河戸畔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Arakawatobime|qq=}}, a member of the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|lt=Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|lt=Kikoku no Miyatsuko|ja|紀国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kikoku no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 紀伊国造}} clan. She became a consort of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, bearing the children {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|ja|豊城入彦命|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|qid=Q11633375|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}} and {{ill|Toyosukiiri-hime|ja|豊鍬入姫命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyosukiiri-hime|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyosukiiri-hime|qq=}}.
== Scholarly Analysis ==
According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} and other sources, Tōtsu Ayume Maguwashi Hime was listed as a consort of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}. She bore Prince {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|ja|豊城入彦命|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|qid=Q11633375|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}, whose royal succession eligibility was compared to his half-brother, Ikume no Mikoto, later known as {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}}. However, it has been argued that the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|lt=Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|lt=Kikoku no Miyatsuko|ja|紀国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kikoku no Miyatsuko|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 紀伊国造}} clan traditionally did not intermarry with the imperial family, raising questions about the historicity of this claim.<ref>{{ill|Toshio Hōga|lt=Toshio Hōga|lt=Hōga Toshio|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hōga Toshio|qq=}}, "The Early Stages of the Keno Clan," in ''Studies on Ancient Clans XVII: The Keno Clan,'' Aogaki Publishing, 2021, pp. 31-33.</ref>
This theory posits that the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Keno clan|ja|毛野氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Keno clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}} may have shared ancestry with the {{ill|Omononushi|lt=Miwa clan|ja|三輪君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omononushi|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, evidenced by shared elements in naming conventions and religious practices, such as the worship of {{ill|Miwa deity|ja|三輪神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa deity|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and its widespread association with the {{ill|Raiden Shrine|ja|雷電神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Raiden Shrine|qq=}} network in the region. It has been suggested that the maternal lineage of {{ill|Mimorowake|ja|御諸別命|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omorowake no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 御諸別王}}, a descendant of the Keno clan, included a daughter of Arakawatobime.<ref>Hōga Toshio, "The Role of Keno and Related Clans in Ancient Japanese Society," in ''Studies on Ancient Clans XVII,'' Aogaki Publishing, 2021, pp. 55-77.</ref>
